judged_text: Format drift between writer and comparator: blacklisted emails are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`) but guest emails are compared raw (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so a guest entered as `User@Example.com` never matches a blacklist entry stored as `user@example.com`. The blacklist filter silently fails to match mixed-case input, letting blacklisted addresses be added as attendees; same asymmetry applies to the existing-attendee dedup (`guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive), so `Bob@x.com` is re-added when `bob@x.com` already attends, producing duplicate attendee rows.

The blacklist filter silently fails to match mixed-case input, letting blacklisted addresses be added as attendees; same asymmetry applies to the existing-attendee dedup (`guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive), so `Bob@x.com` is re-added when `bob@x.com` already attends, producing duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`email.toLowerCase()`), but the filter compares raw `guest` strings (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so mixed-case input like `User@Example.com` won’t match a lowercase blacklist entry and can be added. The same case-sensitive comparison is used for dedup against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`), allowing duplicates differing only by case to be created via `createMany`.
